title: Detection of Spearphishing Link
summary: This detection strategy covers spearphishing links, where an adversary sends a targeted message containing a link to a credential harvesting page or a payload download. It matters because the link is the delivery mechanism for the most common initial access path and because the delivery event is visible in mail gateway records hours or minutes before a user clicks it. The telemetry that makes it possible includes mail gateway message events with sender and recipient, URL rewrite and click time logs, web proxy records showing the redirect chain and the page category, and endpoint process records for the browser or document reader that launched a download. It fails in practice because legitimate marketing and link tracking services generate the same rewrite and redirect pattern, and because internal forwarded mail breaks the original sender context.

beginner.definition: A spearphishing link is a link in a message written for one person or team. It leads to a fake login page or to a harmful download. This detection looks at the message, the click and the download as one chain.
beginner.whyItMatters: Email remains the easiest way into most networks. A message that names your project and your manager is hard to dismiss. The link is the part that turns a message into an intrusion. You can catch it before the click, at the click, or at the download. Each point gives you a chance to block and to warn the targeted staff.
howItWorks: Your mail gateway writes an event for each message, with the sender, the recipient and the rewritten links it found.
When a user clicks, the link protection service or the web proxy records the click and the final address it redirected to.
The rule links the message and the click by the message identifier and the recipient address.
It adds context such as the age of the destination domain, the reputation category and any download that followed.
An alert then shows the original message, the click time, the destination and the affected user in one place.
beginner.example: Think of a postal room that photographs every parcel. A parcel that arrives in the morning and is opened in the staff canteen five minutes later by the person named on the label is normal. The same parcel opened by someone else, at a different building, with the contents posted on again, is worth a call.
takeaways: Link the message record to the click record, because either one alone is weak evidence.
The age of the destination domain is one of the strongest single indicators.
Blocking at click time is fast, but you must also check whether anyone already entered credentials.

objectives: Explain the stages of a spearphishing link attack from message delivery to credential capture
Identify the mail, proxy and endpoint telemetry that records each stage
Correlate a delivered message with a later click and a following download
Assess a suspicious destination using domain age, reputation and redirect behaviour
Execute a containment path that resets exposed credentials and blocks the destination
dataSources: Email gateway message events recording sender, recipient, subject, message identifier and rewritten URLs
Web proxy or secure web gateway logs showing the requested address, the referring page, the redirect target and the category
Endpoint process creation records showing a browser or document reader launching a downloaded file
Domain registration and reputation feed data giving the age and history of the destination domain
logic: The pattern is a delivered message whose rewritten link is clicked within a short time, where the destination resolves through one or more redirects and the final domain is newly registered or categorised as uncategorised, especially when a script interpreter or document reader then starts from the browser. The fields to correlate are the recipient address, the message identifier, the click timestamp, the redirect chain, the final host and the process that followed. The benign case is a known marketing platform using its own tracking domain with an established registration history, while the malicious case shows a lookalike domain under a rarely used top level name, several rapid redirects and a file write followed by execution.
pseudoQuery:
# title: Click on redirect chain to newly registered domain with later download
# logsource:
#   product: network
#   service: proxy
# detection:
#   selection:
#     event_type: http_request
#     http_response|startswith: '3'
#     domain_age_days: < 30
#   selection_down:
#    event_type: process_created
#     image|endswith:
#       - '.exe'
#       - '.js'
#       - '.lnk'
#     parent_image|endswith:
#       - '\\outlook.exe'
#       - '\\chrome.exe'
#   filter:
#     domain|endswith: approved_link_tracking_domains
#   condition: (selection or selection_down) and not filter
# level: high
falsePositives: A marketing campaign that uses a short lived tracking domain and redirects through two hops to the landing page
A file sharing service that sends a link which resolves to a one time download address
A software vendor that publishes a release through a link shortener included in a notification email
An internal newsletter whose click tracking domain is newly created by the communications team
tuningNotes: Allow list your approved link tracking and file sharing domains by name rather than by category, because categorisation lags behind new services. Baseline which applications in your estate normally start from a browser and suppress the few that do so legitimately. Narrowing to the endpoint download half of the rule greatly reduces noise but loses the credential harvesting case where nothing is downloaded, so keep both halves in the same rule with clear alert naming so analysts can tell them apart.
